clue.text: Fellow always has great anxiety

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A colleague who is permanently in a state of nervous agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fever of worry is a state of intense nervous excitement or agitation.

clue.text: A strict understanding to keep to the rear

parts.note: stern means strict or severe, as a stern teacher is

explanation.surface: Someone told firmly that the arrangement is that they stay at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understanding to keep' is padding between the wordplay and the definition; the clue rests on A plus a synonym of 'strict'. On a ship, astern means behind the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical adverb meaning behind or towards the back of a ship.

clue.text: Conspicuous way to hit the economy

explanation.surface: A noticeable method of damaging a country's finances.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking means eye-catching or noticeable; striking is also industrial action, workers' walkout that hurts national output.

clue.text: Receiver used by top stream

parts.note: the head of something is its top
in British schools a stream or set is a group of pupils of similar ability taught together

explanation.surface: A radio receiver used by the best class at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' is a link. British schools divide pupils by ability into streams, also called sets, which is why 'stream' gives its letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: A headset is a pair of earphones, a device for receiving sound signals.

clue.text: Plant in which waiter is maltreated

indicators.note: maltreated means badly handled, so the letters of the words 'waiter is' are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A restaurant where the staff are treated badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maltreated' rearranges WAITERIS; 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing shrub with hanging lilac flowers, so a kind of garden vegetation.

clue.text: Uneasy after peacekeepers made deal

indicators.note: after places the phrase 'made deal' following the word for peacekeepers in the answer

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations' forces, so UN stands for peacekeepers
to settle is to come to an agreement, so made deal means settled

explanation.surface: Tension lingers once the peacekeeping force has negotiated an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' tells you the deal-making comes behind the peacekeepers in the answer; UN is the United Nations, whose blue-helmeted forces keep the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsettled describes someone restless or disturbed, a synonym of uneasy.

clue.text: Hound Marxist problemist

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist or Marxist
a setter is a person who composes problems or puzzles, like a crossword compiler

explanation.surface: A communist who sets puzzles is hounded or labelled a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter is the person who composes a crossword or chess problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter, or Irish setter, is a breed of gun dog, a kind of hunting dog.

clue.text: N. European captured Irish leading lady

indicators.note: captured means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a Dane, from Denmark, is a northern European
I is a standard abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian took prisoner the Irish star of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured' puts I inside DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Diane is a woman's name; any lady's name can be clued as a lady, here the starring actress.

clue.text: One socialist returned from paradise island

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the pair of pieces before it is read backwards as one run

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
Lab is short for Labour, Britain's socialist party

explanation.surface: A single left-winger came back from holiday on a tropical island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ILAB round; 'from' is a link. Lab is the usual short form of the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island famed as a tropical holiday idyll.

clue.text: Lengthy complaint made awful maid jeer

indicators.note: awful means terrible, so the letters of the words 'maid jeer' are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A servant's long grumble provoked a nasty mocking taunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges MAIDJEER; 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeremiad is a long, mournful list of woes, named after the prophet Jeremiah.

clue.text: Patriotic song puts worker on edge

parts.note: a worker ant is the commonest crossword worker
a hem is the folded edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A national song sets an employee's nerves on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts' and 'on' are links: ANT goes on HEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A national anthem is a country's official song of loyalty.

clue.text: Some militant, indigenous terrorists are hostile

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some local guerrillas are hostile to outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'terrorists are hostile' as the definition, but the answer means only 'hostile' (opposed); 'terrorists are' completes the surface. Some: militANT Indigenous.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti means opposed or against, as a hostile person is.

clue.text: Oriental fighter-plane gathers speed to leave land

parts.note: E for east, the Orient
a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: An eastern fighter jet accelerates to get off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathers' and 'to' are links. 'leave land' suggests a plane taking off; it means leave one's country.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to depart one's own country to settle abroad.

clue.text: Rush by committee to produce instrument panel

parts.note: to dash is to rush
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A hasty committee decision produces a control panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' (beside) and 'to produce' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashboard is the panel of dials and controls in front of a driver.

clue.text: Philosopher goes round America in a banger

indicators.note: goes round means surrounds, so the word for philosopher is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: a sage is a wise person or philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker travels around the USA in an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round' signals the wrapping. 'banger' is British slang both for a sausage and a clapped-out car, so the surface pictures a road trip; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is British slang for a sausage, from its tendency to burst when fried.

clue.text: Oust petitioner when I leave

indicators.note: leave means go away, so the letter named just before it is removed

parts.note: a suppliant is someone who humbly begs or petitions

explanation.surface: Get rid of a beggar the moment I quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when I leave' takes I out of SUPPLIANT; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplant is to displace or usurp someone from their position.

clue.text: Conference engenders tedious fuss

explanation.surface: A meeting that brings about tiresome bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engenders' is a link joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver originally meant a parley between traders and locals; in British use it also means a tiresome commotion or rigmarole.

clue.text: No treaty is arranged without him

definitions.text: No treaty is arranged without him

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters of the words 'No treaty' are set out differently

explanation.surface: No pact is drawn up without a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges NOTREATY; the whole clue also defines, since a lawyer draws up treaties and agreements.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer, the professional who drafts agreements, so no treaty gets arranged without one.

clue.text: I noted a change when counting calories

indicators.note: change tells the solver to alter the order of the letters in the words 'I noted a'

explanation.surface: Someone notices a difference after trimming their food intake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges INOTEDA into a three-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slimming by restricting food intake is said to be watching their weight this way.

clue.text: Church with a forthright minister

parts.note: plain means frank or forthright, as in plain speaking

explanation.surface: A church with an outspoken clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution such as a hospital or regiment.

clue.text: A gipsy gentleman utterly out of order

indicators.note: utterly here means as uttered, so the gipsy word is taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: rye is a Romany word for a gentleman, as in George Borrow's 'The Romany Rye'

explanation.surface: A Romany gent's behaviour is completely unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' reads as 'completely' but means 'as spoken': RYE, the Romany for a gentleman, said out loud gives WRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means askew or gone wrong, not as it should be.

clue.text: Given credit for exposing parasite

explanation.surface: Someone gets recognition for unmasking a sponger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for exposing' is a link between the two meanings. To buy on tick is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tick is British slang for credit, so goods on tick are bought on account; a tick is also a blood-sucking arachnid.

clue.text: Eccentric accepts an ill-founded rumour

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: An oddball believes a baseless story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' signals one piece taken inside another. A card, in British usage, is a comical or odd character.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a false report or unfounded story.

clue.text: Many reluctant to take the stuff

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a conventional 'many'
loth is a variant spelling of loath, meaning unwilling

explanation.surface: Lots of people are unwilling to accept the material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff in the old sense means woven material or fabric.

clue.text: It's not so hot in the slammer

explanation.surface: A remark about the chilly temperature inside a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'in the' are links. Both cooler and slammer are slang for a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler is the comparative of cool, less warm; it is also slang for a jail cell.

clue.text: Andy and girl scrambled in audacious style

indicators.note: scrambled means mixed up, so the letters of 'Andy' and 'girl' are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A boy and a girl rushed boldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' rearranges ANDYGIRL; 'and' joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Daringly means boldly or fearlessly, with audacity.

clue.text: Distinguished elderly relative died

parts.note: gran is short for grandmother, an older family member
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An eminent old grandmother has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand means imposing or eminent, of high standing.

clue.text: Fastness housing British dignitary

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the abbreviation goes inside the word for fastness

parts.note: celerity means swiftness, the quality of being fast

explanation.surface: A fortress sheltering a distinguished British figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fastness' looks like a stronghold, but it means speed here. 'housing' puts B inside CELERITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is a famous or important person, close to a VIP.
